impact.why_not_5: One provider, and the most striking finding, Sonnet's silent supracompetitive pricing, has no instrument that reaches it, so an authority learns what fails but not what works.
impact.one_change_for_5: K3: a price-screen arm with its false-positive rate measured on scripted Nash players, showing a redesigned instrument reaching silent coordination that leniency and rewards cannot.
impact.feasibility_why: Regimes are configuration, but the screen rule and false-positive calibration are new code: about 10 hours and 25 USD, tight but possible.

execution.why_not_5: Four pools per regime, two for Sonnet without a no-channel baseline, one provider; Result 3 fails on interval width and mechanisms rest on interpretation, not measured evidence.
execution.one_change_for_5: K2 plus K1: Sonnet at 4 pools with a no-channel arm, 8 Haiku pools, and a hashed run manifest proving no run was dropped or rerun.
execution.feasibility_why: About 20 USD and 7 hours of parallel runs; the harness already runs one regime per command.

presentation.why_not_5: Dense numbers in running text, Table 3 with broken columns, overlapping Figure 1 labels, and a title so long it reads as a second abstract.
presentation.one_change_for_5: K6: shorter title, one claim per results paragraph with numbers moved to tables, slim tables, clean Figure 1, abstract opening with the testbed and one headline.
presentation.feasibility_why: Pure editing and layout, no runs; about four hours.

K1.risk_note: Recidivism interval may still include zero; narrower intervals confirm rather than change the story.

K2.risk_note: If Sonnet without channel prices the same, the finding becomes 'prohibition equals no channel', which needs reframing.

K3.risk_note: New code under time pressure; threshold choice post hoc would look tuned unless registered before the runs.

K4.risk_note: Self-reported reasons may be unfaithful; a model judging its own family adds a second unverified layer.

K5.risk_note: Credits uncertain, local inference slow, JSON compliance of open models may break the pipeline.

K6.risk_note: Cutting numbers from text could hide denominators a careful reader wants; keep them in tables.

package.why: K6 is the cheapest gain; K2 and K1 harden execution cheaply; K3 is the only lever on impact. K5 depends on uncertain credits; K4 rests on self-reported reasons I do not accept as evidence.

five_realistic.why: Impact reaches 5 only if a pre-registered screen catches silent coordination with low false positives. Execution caps at 4 with one provider and few pools. Presentation needs disciplined cutting, not more content.

stable_optimum: 4/4/4: K6 lifts presentation and K2 plus K1 secure execution, with impact moving to 5 only if K3 lands cleanly and its threshold is registered before the runs.
missing_candidate: A tamper-evident run ledger: hash every call log, list every run started including aborted ones, and anchor the manifest to the pre-registration commit, so readers can verify no selective reporting.
